title: The Lock That Kept Its Word
logline: When a Hartsford herbalist hires Jory Brennick to pull his grandmother's sealed chest from a collapsed house before the dock crew's new pilings seal it away for good, the lock guarding it opens exactly as the old stories promised, and exacts exactly the price they warned of.
promise: A race against a building schedule through a collapsed drowned house, a lock that costs precisely what the old chant says it costs, and a recovered remedy from before the Cataclysm that proves its worth in the present.
setting: the drowned streets below Hartsford and Shoreside, Sunken Reach, early autumn, about twenty years after the Cataclysm

cast.name: Jory Brennick
cast.want: to prove himself a salvager worth hiring on his own name, not just as Maud's son

cast.name: Maud Brennick
cast.want: to keep her son from underestimating the danger of the drowned streets she still remembers from before the flood
cast.appearance: auburn hair just starting to grey
cast.dress: short trousers, long sleeves, wide-brimmed hat

cast.name: Walter Ames
cast.station: Hartsford herbalist, descendant of the drowned town's apothecary family
cast.want: to recover his grandmother's sealed chest of remedies before the entrance is lost, hoping its cures can ease a fever moving through Hartsford
cast.appearance: A stooped man of sixty-one with a close white beard and ink-stained fingers from years of grinding herbs.
cast.dress: A patched wool coat over a leather apron, a brass magnifying loupe on a cord at his neck.
cast.voice_note: soft-spoken, apologizes before asking for anything

cast.name: Selah Vance
cast.station: Shoreside dock-builder, foreman of the stilt expansion crew
cast.want: to drive the new pilings and finish the stilt line before the first winter storm closes the harbor to construction
cast.appearance: A tall, broad-shouldered woman of thirty-eight with wind-cracked skin and dark hair cropped short under a canvas cap.
cast.dress: A heavy oiled coat and tall boots, a carpenter's plumb-line looped at her belt.
cast.voice_note: brisk, states facts rather than opinions

cast.name: Liora Quill
cast.want: to land a find notable enough that people stop calling her 'Jory's partner'
cast.appearance: A lean young woman of nineteen with a long braid of light brown hair, bleached pale at the tips by sun and salt.
cast.dress: A sleeveless diving vest over rolled trousers, a string of small brass fittings tied at her belt.

chapters.title: Six Days Before the Pilings
beats: Jory and Liora Quill sort the morning's salvage on a Floatsome platform, trading jabs about whose haul is better.
Walter Ames arrives by hired boat from Hartsford, asking the dockhands specifically for Jory by name.

Walter explains that Shoreside's dock crew will drive new pilings into his family's old street in six days, sealing the collapsed house's entrance forever, and he needs his grandmother's locked chest of remedies out before then.
Maud, overhearing, warns that stretch of street lies close to the new fissure and hasn't been checked since a tremor loosened the harbor shelf.
Jory accepts the contract over Maud's objection, setting a six-day race against the builders' schedule.

chapters.title: The Foreman's Schedule
beats: Jory, Liora, and Maud travel to Shoreside to confirm the timeline with foreman Selah Vance.
Selah states plainly that her crew starts driving pilings into that exact street in six days, and she won't delay the work for a salvage job.
Selah adds that an early storm moving in from the coast could push her start forward to five days, or fewer.
Maud unrolls her old hazard chart of the drowned street, drawn from memory, marking the house, but admits she hasn't checked it since the tremor.
At dawn they dive to the site and find the street doesn't match the chart: the house's roof has collapsed into the lane since Maud last saw it.

chapters.title: Through the Broken Window
beats: Jory and Liora find the entrance marked on Maud's chart fully blocked by fallen roof timbers.
They find another way in, through a broken parlor window into the sunken room.
Inside, they find fresh chisel marks on a wall near the strongbox, chipped away far too recently to be from the Cataclysm.
They locate the strongbox bolted to a support beam, its lock seamless, no keyhole, faintly warm through Jory's glove.
Running low on air, they surface unable to open or free it, left wondering who else has been down there before them.

chapters.title: The Foreman's Survey
beats: Jory reports the fresh chisel marks to Walter, who has no idea who could have gotten inside.
Selah Vance, checking their progress at the dock, admits her own survey crew probed that exact house last week while marking piling positions, chipping at the wall to test the foundation.
Selah reveals her survey found the collapsed house sits directly where a new piling line is meant to go, meaning the piling itself could crush the box before it's ever opened.

Walter explains the box was sealed generations ago by his grandmother, an herbalist, using material drawn from the fissure, and that the lock opens only to a blood relative who speaks the household's true name three times.
He admits the old stories say the lock 'takes its own payment' for opening, though no one living has used it, and insists he must be the one to speak it himself.

chapters.title: What Maud Remembers
beats: Jory relays the chant requirement and the lock's warmth to Maud back at Floatsome.
Maud realizes she once heard children chanting something at that very door as a girl, before the Cataclysm, a phrase spoken for luck at the threshold.
She recalls enough of its shape to know it named the household three times, matching what Walter described.
Maud warns that a lock drawing on fissure material might ask for more than the old stories admit, since nobody has tested one in twenty years, and insists on coming along to watch.
A runner arrives from Shoreside: the storm has moved in faster than expected, and Selah's crew now starts driving pilings in three days, not six.

chapters.title: The Second Dive
beats: With three days left, Jory, Liora, Maud, and Walter take a boat out together at first light.
They guide a nervous Walter down through the collapsed house to the strongbox.
Walter speaks the remembered chant, naming his family's name three times as Maud recalls it.
The lock answers by drawing warmth through his hand, his fingers going numb and cold as the box finally opens.
Inside is not the ready chest of remedies he expected, but a slim, water-stained formulary and a separate wrapped bundle of unfamiliar mineral.

chapters.title: A Different Kind of Cure
beats: Onshore, Walter's numb hand slowly warms while Maud examines the bundle, recognizing the mineral as raw fissure-glass, the same substance worked into the lock itself.

They read the water-stained formulary together, Jory sounding out passages where the ink has run, learning Walter's grandmother used tiny amounts of that mineral in her remedies decades before anyone understood what it was.
Walter admits this complicates his hope for an easy cure, since the notes call for careful, exact measures, and the mineral is costly and dangerous to handle.
Liora spots one clear page listing a measured recipe for an emergency fever draught already proven safe once before, if a sample can be matched exactly to the one in the bundle.
Walter decides to carry the formulary and the mineral straight to a Hartsford healer rather than try it himself, racing what time is left before the storm.

chapters.title: The Pilings Go In
beats: Three days later, the Hartsford healer tests the old fever draught on a patient and it eases the outbreak, using the exact measure from the grandmother's formulary.
Selah's crew drives the first pilings into the cleared street exactly on schedule, the strongbox and its contents already safely out.
Walter pays Jory the full contract fee and gives Maud a share for her memory of the chant and her corrected chart.
Maud marks the collapsed roof and the fissure's nearer reach onto her chart, so the next salvager won't be caught out as they were.
Jory and Liora, pleased with the finished job, start eyeing the fissure itself as their next contract, with Maud cautiously agreeing to chart the way this time.

notes: let's look at jory in the sunken reach with either someone contracting him to find something and he discovering  a mystery.
